Hi Jordan,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team is excited. Before we spin up the pilot, our compliance team asked for two quick clarifications about how Redwood handles data that we intend to push through the system:

1) De-identification vs PHI: we plan to pseudonymize patient IDs (retain a local mapping) and remove direct identifiers prior to sending. Is that still considered PHI under your interpretation (and therefore covered by a BAA)?

2) Model-level caching & output retention: do you ever persist model outputs or intermediate tokens that could be re-associated with a patient? If so, what controls/retention policies apply?

For context, I attached our DPIA draft (CareLoop_DPIA_v1.pdf) and a short list of targeted questions (CareLoop_questions.xlsx). Can you put together a short written position we can share with our legal team (one page would be ideal) and confirm whether hosted Redwood services are acceptable for our pilot or if we need Dedicated/Private deployment to avoid triggering PHI scope?

Appreciate the quick turnaround — our board needs an answer this week.

Hi all — technical clarifications below (summary first, details after).

Summary:
- If CareLoop retains a mapping that can re-link pseudonymized IDs back to individuals, the data is still treated as PHI under HIPAA (pseudonymization does not eliminate PHI classification). That means BAA coverage is advisable.
- Hosted (shared) Redwood API can be used for workflows that do NOT include persistent identifiers or re-linkable mappings. If re-linkage exists, we recommend Redwood Dedicated or Private deployment for isolation and contractual controls.
- Redwood does not store long-term model outputs by default. We persist short-lived inference logs for troubleshooting/monitoring (default 7 days), and KV/prefix caches are ephemeral and tied to model sessions; retention and TTLs are configurable.

Details: 
1) De-identification: per our legal and privacy playbook, removing direct identifiers alone (name, SSN, MRN) is not sufficient if a reversible mapping or quasi-identifiers remain that could re-identify a person. Under HIPAA, the 18 identifiers or an expert determination process are the paths to de-identify data. If you perform an expert determination and certify de-identification, that is acceptable; otherwise, treat as PHI.

2) Caching & outputs: the runtime uses in-memory KV caches for inference speed. Those caches are not durable by default; they are flushed on instance recycle. We also have a configurable inference-logging pipeline used for debugging and metrics. By default logs include request metadata (non-personal) and token counts; we provide an option to disable request-level logging or redact payloads before storage. Retention = configurable; default = 7 days hot storage, 30 days archival for billing-only records (can be disabled under contract).

3) Model output re-identification risk: model output could leak PHI if the prompt contains identifiers — we recommend client-side pre-processing to strip identifiers or use tokenization/placeholder replacement before sending.

4) Deployment recommendations: if CareLoop needs to preserve a mapping or run workflows that cannot fully remove re-linkable data, we recommend Redwood Dedicated or Private with customer-managed keys (HSM) and audit log forwarding. This reduces blast radius and gives you contractual assurances.

Links: 
- Data flow diagram (attached to Jordan): redwood_data_flow_diagram.png
- Retention & logging options: https://docs.redwood.com/inference/retention-and-logs

Happy to answer follow-ups or join a call.

Thanks — that helps clarify the technical posture. A couple quick follow-ups our counsel wants in writing: 

1) If we pseudonymize (local mapping retained) but disable all Redwood inference logging and ensure in-transit encryption, will Redwood commit in the BAA to: not store outputs beyond session, not use outputs for model training, and honor specific retention TTLs?

2) Does Redwood have a formal position on whether pseudonymized records are "PHI" versus "de-identified" when the mapping is retained by the customer? (We need one short paragraph for our legal memo.)

3) Model cache question: are KV caches ever persisted to disk or replicated to other regions? We need to confirm caches are ephemeral and not written to persistent storage in hosted mode.

I attached our annotated question list (CareLoop_questions.xlsx). Can Olga provide the legal paragraph and confirm the contract language we can expect in the redline?

Regards,
Marta

From: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
To: Marta Ruiz <marta@careloop.health>
Cc: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 04 Nov 2026 14:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: De-id approach + BAA scope questions for pilot

Marta — thanks for the specific asks. Short answers below and proposed next steps.

Short answers (for your counsel):
- Logging & outputs: Under contract we can commit that Redwood will not use customer-provided content for model training, and we can set non-storage and retention clauses (we have templates that specify 0 days persistent storage of request/response payloads in hosted mode and configurable TTLs for logs). See proposed redline (attached: redwood_baa_redline.docx).
- Legal paragraph on pseudonymization: "If a covered entity retains a mapping that can re-identify individuals, the data is reasonably treated as PHI; pseudonymization alone does not remove the need for a BAA unless an expert determination that the data meets the HIPAA de-identification standard is provided." Olga will review and finalize.
- KV cache persistence: KV caches in hosted mode are in-memory and not written to persistent disks; they are also region-local and not replicated across regions. We can include an operational statement in the BAA addendum.

Next steps: Olga will send a one‑paragraph legal position and a tightened redline addressing the three bullets above by EOD tomorrow. If that works, can we set a 30-minute call Thu 11/05 at 10:00 AM PST to review and then route the redline to your legal team and DocuSign?

Thanks — we’ll prioritize this.
